component.name: Negs
component.summary: Develop photographs with a physical simulation of film

description.p: Negs runs your pictures through a physical simulation of film: the dyes, the print paper, the glow around highlights and the grain. They come out looking shot on film, not filtered to look like it.
It is built on the spektrafilm spectral film model and its GPU port, spektrafilm-rs. Every slider updates the preview live, and what you see is what you export.

ul.li: Opens RAW files from most cameras, plus JPEG, TIFF and PNG with their colour profiles
Pick from dozens of colour and black-and-white film stocks and print papers
Crop, straighten, and add borders with each stock's real edge print
Image Size enlarges a photo before the film, so grain forms at print size
Save, apply, import and export film and Lab presets
Exports PNG, TIFF or JPEG at 8 or 16 bits with EXIF and an embedded ICC profile
Fast GPU exports, with a 64-bit reference render for the most exact result
Export the current film and paper as a .cube LUT

screenshot.caption: Developing a photograph with the film, camera and print controls

description.p: The native per-user bundle now includes OpenBLAS, so the engine starts without a separate OpenBLAS installation.
Negs for Linux is now available as a Flatpak and an AppImage for any x86_64 distribution.

ul.li: Open Folder shows every photograph in a folder in the film strip
A Presets page saves, applies, imports and exports film and Lab presets
Reference exports are about 30% faster on the CPU

description.p: Presets on Mac and Windows, and colour-managed input and previews on every platform.
